docs.radio.a11y.disabled: disabled is for an option that is not available: it is dimmed, shows a not-allowed cursor, and assistive technology reads it as unavailable. There is no read-only radio.
docs.radio.a11y.focus: Keyboard focus is drawn with the focus ring token around the control, also when the option is selected, where the brand color alone would not show it. A click does not draw it.
docs.radio.a11y.group: Put the options of a group in a fieldset with a legend that says what the group chooses, and give every option the same name. A screen reader then reads the legend with each option, and the browser treats the options as one group.
docs.radio.a11y.keyboard: Tab enters the group once: on the selected option, or on the first one when none is selected. The arrow keys move to the next or the previous option, wrap around at the ends, skip a disabled option and select the one they land on. Space selects the focused option.
docs.radio.a11y.native: It is a native radio input inside its label: a click on the text selects the option, the text is its accessible name, and the grouping, the keys and the form value come from the browser, not from the library.
docs.radio.a11y.selected: A selected option shows a dot inside a filled circle, so the state does not rest on color alone, and assistive technology reads it from the native checked state.
docs.radio.a11y.strings: Radio has no text of its own: the label and the legend are yours, in the language of your page, and a FormaProvider changes nothing here.
docs.radio.a11y.target: The whole label is the target: its row is 36 px high, and 44 px below 768 px of width.
docs.radio.api.className: Added to the label, which holds the box and the text, and not to the input: every other attribute goes to the input. It is the other way round from Input, where className goes to the input.
docs.radio.api.label: The text of the option. It is what names the radio, and a click on it selects the option.
docs.radio.api.others: Every other attribute of the native input element goes to it as it is: name, value, checked, defaultChecked, onChange, disabled, required, id, style, aria-*, the event handlers and ref. It takes no type, which is always radio, and no children.
docs.radio.controlled.description: With checked and onChange on every option, the parent owns the selection from one value: it can show it somewhere else, or refuse a change. Without them, the browser keeps it.
docs.radio.controlled.hint: The line under the group reads the state of the parent.
docs.radio.controlled.title: Controlled
docs.radio.limit.contrast: The border of an option that is not selected is the line color, the same as the border of Input, and it is faint against the page: under the 3:1 that WCAG asks of the edge of a control. Its shape and its label still tell the options apart, but a stronger border is a pending design decision.
docs.radio.limit.design: The design has no Radio frame: its look follows Resolve, and the checkbox of the design is the nearest reference (it spaces the label 8 px from the control and dims a disabled one to 55%, where Radio keeps the 12 px and 45% of Resolve). Aligning them is a pending design decision.
docs.radio.limit.group: There is no group component: the fieldset, its legend, the layout and the spacing between the options are yours, and a lone Radio lays out as an inline row.
docs.radio.limit.messages: A radio has no hint, error or required marker of its own. Put them in text near the group and link it to the options with aria-describedby.
docs.radio.limit.names: Radios that share a name are one group wherever they are, in the same form or, with no form, in the whole document. Give each group a name of its own: the examples on this page take one from useId.
docs.radio.limit.readOnly: There is no read-only radio: the browser ignores readOnly on it. Show a value that cannot change as text, and use disabled only for an option that is not available.
docs.radio.limit.size: There is one size: a 20 px control with an 8 px dot, and a row 36 px high, which is 44 px below 768 px of width.
docs.radio.state.defaultCheckedHint: One option starts selected, and Tab enters the group on it.
docs.radio.state.defaultHint: Nothing is selected: Tab enters the group on its first option.
docs.radio.state.disabledHint: An option that is not available: it leaves the tab order, the arrow keys skip it and a form does not send it.
docs.radio.states.description: The states that Radio has today. A group is one choice at a time: an option is selected or it is not, and it can be disabled when it is not available. All of it works here: click an option, or press Tab and then the arrow keys.
docs.radio.summary: One option of a group, on a native radio input: the group takes one choice and the browser moves between the options.
docs.radio.usage.description: Import Radio and give each option a label, the same name and its own value. Put the group in a fieldset with a legend that says what it chooses.
